key_insight: The paper shows that grammar-aware quantum NLP can be adapted beyond English to Hindi by modeling Hindi syntax and negation with compositional quantum circuits for sentiment classification.
engineering_relevance: This work suggests a practical path for building language-specific quantum NLP pipelines for morphologically rich, low-resource languages.
method: Manually annotated Hindi sentiment dataset with positive, negative, and neutral labels
Encoded sentences with pregroup grammar and a negation-aware compositional grammar in Lambeq
Trained hybrid quantum neural networks for binary and ternary sentiment tasks
evidence_signal: The abstract reports effective sentiment classification on the annotated Hindi dataset using both binary and ternary evaluation setups.
watch_item: Performance may depend strongly on manual grammar design and annotated data quality, which can limit scalability to broader Hindi text domains.
paper_title: Extending the Frontiers of QNLP Beyond English: Grammar-Sensitive Pipeline for Hindi Sentiment Classification Using Compositional Quantum Models
